named_subject: a long-necked four-legged animal, read as a horse or dog
action: The animal stands facing left with its head raised, turns to face right, lowers its head forward, lifts it again, and ends with its head lowered toward the bucket.
identity_gap: Frames 1-5 match the doodle's head, eye, neck and rectangular rump closely, but from frame 13 on the rump rectangle is drawn twice, overlapping, so the body looks doubled.
notes: The film shows a dog looking up at a person, turning, walking toward the camera and then sniffing down at the bowl; the animation gets the start pose and the final head-down at the bucket, but the turn happens as a mirror flip in a single frame (5 to 6), frame 8 stretches the body, and frame 10 shrinks it. The one change that would help most is to animate the turn across several in-between frames instead of flipping the drawing, and remove the duplicated rump strokes.
